Levin, "Membrane voltage and connexin expression work together to enhance tumor growth and metastasis in cancer", bioRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.09.02.748840, version 1, 3 September 2026, CC-BY 4.0. It asks how strongly gap junctions must couple cells for healthy tissue to turn a tumour back to the healthy state. The user gave the work the highest priority on 17 November 2026 (D207), and its driver and its note are on main since that evening. Its linear model runs as written on the engine's own pieces, the reactions operator with the passive routes' neutral law on junction routes, unqualified, and its error against dense solves falls at second order; its exact Norton-equivalent network on the tissue model's own routes is its check. The preprint's tissue tables need engine features not built yet: a charged microRNA on junctions, a two-state junction gate and larger field solves (FR-15 to FR-17). On a line of 25 cells, the first six a tumour, the driver searched for the coupling at which the tumour returns to the healthy state; an engine check first stopped that search (FR-19), and after its fix the search ran again from main, followed by a ladder of ten couplings and a 9 by 9 sheet, an extension beyond the preprint's setup. On 18 November 2026 the user answered the note's questions (D219). Its next bundle, for a free seat: the correctly specified 25 by 25 threshold case, the preprint's Figure 5a through the windowed execution and record path, and BITSEY run unmodified, out of process, for pinned reference outputs, after its licence and revision are checked; the 2D search's registration states its geometry, success criterion, horizon, bracket, refinement rule and compute budget before it runs. Two judged comparisons were approved, each under a registered protocol with code-blind references: the linear model's numerical qualification, Figure 8 judged against independently derived physical balances, with the printed recursion's discrepancy kept as a finding; and the threshold comparison, whose verdict includes successful refinement and a convergence condition declared in advance, and in which only the 2D field is a true pre-registration, since the 1D line's value was already seen. For Table 3, its logged inputs and the interventions as actually executed govern the code's target, and the printed table is kept as a separate publication target, with the mapping discrepancies reported. FR-15 to FR-17 were scheduled with the owners whose files they touch, not yet started. The same evening the user put the core and the feature requests first (D222): the bundle's steps 2 to 5 and the references for the two judged comparisons wait for free seats and lanes. On 19 November 2026 charged species in the species operators, which the work's microRNA needs, were scheduled into the core pass as a general feature, starting with a diagnosis (FR-15's F2 part; D226, D228 item 4). By 20 November 2026 its first two steps had landed as general features: charged species in the reactions operator, where every reaction conserves charge, and a charged constant-field route law on the passive routes, on membranes first; hosting it on junctions waits for two answers from the tissue model's owner. Five quick worlds of this work form a set of crossrev, recorded from the engine's source before any core change, which every later core landing must regenerate bit for bit; that holds the engine to its own earlier programs, and compares nothing with the preprint. None of this is judged.

switch.heading: The switch, in plain words
items: Each cell carries a switch made of two molecules that suppress each other: the microRNA miR200 blocks the making of the protein ZEB, and ZEB blocks the making of miR200.
With miR200 high and ZEB low, the cell is epithelial (E), the healthy state here. With ZEB high and miR200 low, it is mesenchymal (M), the tumour state.
Each state sustains itself, which is what makes it a switch.

Only miR200 passes through gap junctions, so healthy neighbours can feed it into a tumour cell. With enough coupling, that tips the cell's switch back to E. With too little, the tumour holds. §7's "neither" search finds that threshold.

standing.says: Protons as a species, a pump that acidifies a compartment against its gradient, and buffering (feature request FR-4), one of the two priority users of the modular rework (D176). Protons are one species whose free part is set by a fast buffer rule at every stage, the proton pump is a transporter on the compartment's membrane, counterions are explicit, and its first case runs on fuel held constant. Its pump, its buffer and a proton leak landed on main with the rework on 16 November 2026, as pieces of the tissue model, together with the drivers that build its first world and the tools for its qualification. Its independent references, written by a separate agent that read no engine code, show the compartment acidifying from pH 7.2 to about 5.1 against its gradient while the cytoplasm stays within 0.02 pH; without the counterion route it stalls. A kernel for treating the compartment's membrane implicitly in the step is on main too, with its tests; no model uses it yet, and chloride and pores wait for it. Its protocol, fr4-acidification-v1, was registered on 17 November 2026, after its rehearsal passed 21 of 21 criteria, and judged once the same day: it passed all 21 judged criteria against the independent references. cards.title: FR-7: abundance to function, in a closed loop
cards.asks: Can a transient template change a protein's abundance, and so a measurable response, in a loop that feeds back on itself?

standing.label: Abundance to function (FR-7)

level.label: Qualified or judged
level.says: Numerically qualified (a registered protocol passed) or judged (used in a registered experiment), in its declared scope.

standing.says: Judged in one scope only: FR-7's first closed loop, its comparison F4 against the code-blind reference R-loop, passed on 20 November 2026; F3's six-world comparison against its own references is queued, and every piece of the loop is development, not judged, on its own part. The request: the amount of a protein in the composite sets how a membrane population conducts, and a declared species can drive the rate at which it is made, so that a transient template changes a measurable response that may or may not outlive it (feature request FR-7). The user's answers of 18 November 2026 set the first loop's unit, admitted the loop through the one routing door, and ruled that a closed loop is not called qualified until a closed feedback case passes beside a control in which the feedback is cut (D217, D218). Its pieces landed on 19 and 20 November 2026: the unit producer, whose removal of units inside itself is a scoped exception to D177 that the user accepted (D232); the coupling operator's version 2, with a factor on another operator's rate and a population's abundance as a source; the producer's assembly rate as a target (F3); declared initial units per maturation pool; and the comparison code, the mappers and comparisons of the chain and of the loop, which has no test of its own. For the closed loop, under the user's delegation, the Na/K pump with Na-leak units at a declared synthetic time scale was chosen (D231), and its world scales the template's half-saturation and dose five-fold (D233). Its world, as its mapper declares it: one cell of the composite over the tissue model @3, with the Na/K pump on held fuel, membrane state's K-leak and Na-leak populations, species turnover, the coupling operator's version 2 and the unit producer. The judged run, from a frozen snapshot of main with the registered interface, ran both arms, closed and clamped: every compared row is within its band, the cut's applied factor is within its registered bound, the clearance row equals the registered 260 s, all 30 persistence rows pass, and the pump's rate read from the engine's own readouts matches its cumulative ledger. Its values are synthetic and labelled so.

standing.says: Development, not judged. The measurements and the harness that come before a long-duration mode is chosen (feature request FR-8), all on today's fine engine. Stage 0 landed on main on 19 November 2026: five measurements, each with its criteria registered before its run, and the harness, a world of an hour whose cue at its midpoint switches a cell for good, run at three steps. Stage 0 makes no qualification claim, since its references are the engine's own runs. A ladder of rungs was then decided, with the user's agreement (D224): rung 0 first, to explain why the fine engine's order of accuracy drops through a switch, before any later rung is registered, and every later accuracy study judged against it. Rung 0 ran the same day, on the tissue model alone. Its registered verdict is "instrument not validated": its control for the slow phase had no power, so no cause is identified. Under an amendment registered blind before the main windows were read, the weaker evidence, the instruments pass and the cause is the transient before the step's order settles: the observed orders climb toward 2 as the step halves. The energy check X2 landed on 19 November 2026 (a part of its own). Rung 1's registered control, today's integrator with X2 on, then ran first, as the user chose (D232): its largest passing steps under the parity caps were 20 ms on the harness's calm stretch, held by charge stability, 1 ms through the cue, by the location rule, and 5 ms on a second world, by the junction-gate bound, and X2 refused nothing. By D232's rules a method was chosen on 20 November 2026 (D235): N2, the design note's linearly implicit step, as rung 1 as registered, then C, a fine-window executor, required and not optional. Rung 0's official verdict stays inconclusive (D232), and the fourth external review's fix makes its reader check each arm's identity, step and grid. Implemented and guarded: on main, with tests of the harness's judge and of the measurements M1, M2, M4 and M5, M1's on a registered world. M3, a measurement of cost, has no test of its own, and neither has rung 0's driver, which the engine's guard for restarts lists as a development tool.
